decisionsTitle: Every mail goes through the outbox, and one road down is no loss: why Gmail «did not send» on QA, the visitors' messages queued, failover between Mailgun and Gmail (amending §149, §676, §772 and §622)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-15, ~10:05**, with a screenshot of «Setări» → «Spune-ne ceva» on QA, all four forms set to Mailgun: «aici nu se trimiteau mailurile prin Gmail-ul clubului… nu înțeleg de ce, dar mergea doar cu Mailgun. Vreau să mă asigur că 1: există un queue de mailuri de trimis și nu se pierd mesaje; 2: dacă pică un serviciu (Mailgun) se trimite prin celălalt (Gmail) și invers.» He had said «YOLO» the day before: the open points below are decided, and said.

**The diagnosis, first (read-only: `vercel api` for the env names, `vercel logs` on both projects, `/api/health?deep=1` on QA).** What is proven: QA has `CONTACT_SMTP_USER` and `CONTACT_SMTP_PASSWORD` (so the card did not grey the road); its function log from 2026-10-14 19:05 to 2026-10-15 06:52 UTC holds eight posts to `/ro/contact/spune-ne`, every one `[feedback] <form> <reader>: sent`, and not one `[feedback] delivery failed` or `smtp <code>` line in seven days — no refusal was ever logged; and the outbox's Gmail road on the same account works (`email.gmail` reads configured, twenty sent in the last day, last failure `smtp ETIMEDOUT` on 2026-09-28, nothing since). So nothing points to a 535-5.7.8, a wrong port, an egress block or an unset variable. **What is not proven is which road carried those eight posts.** The old log line named no road — `sent` is logged alike for Gmail and Mailgun — and the owner's screenshot had all four forms on Mailgun, so all eight may have been Mailgun's; nothing shows that Gmail accepted any of them. «Gmail had accepted every message» is a hypothesis, not a finding. The site could not say, because the direct sender logged `sent` and kept nothing: no road, no id, no time. **A hypothesis for the owner to check in a minute:** a form whose «Către» is the club's own Gmail (the account that sends) is filed by Gmail in Sent / All mail and not necessarily in the Inbox, so a message sent by Gmail to itself looks lost; the card now warns beside the box when the recipient is the sending account. A second difference is gone too: the direct Gmail send never consulted QA's allowlist while Mailgun's road did. **Production's «Scrie-ne»:** the contact form sends only through Gmail; its two posts in seven days were both logged delivered (`[contact] delivered marked as possible spam`), with no failure line, so Google accepted them — and the same «Către = the sending account» check applies to which mailbox shows them.

**Decision.** (1) **One outbox for every mail.** «Scrie-ne» (§149) and the four «Spune-ne ceva» forms (§676, §772) no longer send from the request. Each queues an outbox row — three new message types, `CONTACT_MESSAGE`, `FEEDBACK_MESSAGE` and the platform's own `RELAY_NOTICE`, and three expand-only columns on `email_outbox` (migration `0162_outbox_road_and_failures`: `road`, the club's choice for the form; `road_failures`, what each road did to this message; `body_deleted_at`) — and answers «trimis»; the same request sends it after its response (`drainRelayAfterResponse`, whatever «Când pleacă emailurile» says, up to four passes in thirty seconds), the outbox job sends what is left. A visitor's message has its own worker (`notifications/relay.ts`) and the notifications' claim leaves it alone: it has no template, no participant and a road of its own. The contact form's row carries the club's To, the other recipients as visible copies and the Bcc list; a «Spune-ne ceva» message is one row per recipient. (2) **The words are kept until delivery, never after.** The words travel in `payload_json`; the moment the message leaves they are deleted (`{ "deleted": true }`, `body_deleted_at`) and the row stays as the record — road, road it left by, time, provider id, tries, what each road answered; never an address or a word. So «the site keeps nothing» became «the site keeps a message only until it is delivered — seconds, three days at the very most when no service works (the relay gives up at twenty-four hours, the retention sweep is the net at three days)»: the card's footer, the forms' sentences (`Tell.safety.reader*`, `Tell.privacy*`), `Admin.emails.feedbackForms.roads` and the privacy notice **template**'s contact and feedback paragraphs now say it (template only: the texts in force move when the club approves; the paragraphs carry a marker of their own, `{{relayQueue}}`, and `/admin/tasks` carries the row `relayQueueNotice` — open for as long as the notice in force does not name it in both languages, done by itself the day one does — because the notice in force says «nicio copie», which is untrue for the time a row waits; the queue is not held back for it). The anonymous forms stay anonymous: nothing of the sender beyond what the message carries is stored, and the row is cleaned the same way. (3) **Failover, both ways.** A failure that is the SERVICE's — a refused login (`smtp EAUTH`, Mailgun 401/403), a 5xx, no connection, a spent allowance or a pause — counts against the road for that message; after **two** (decided: one is a hiccup, a second a minute later is a road down) the other road gets its turn, Mailgun to Gmail and Gmail to Mailgun, and the two take turns by their counts after that. The first retries are three and five seconds, so the after-response pass reaches the other road within seconds; then the outbox's own backoff. A road this deployment lacks, or that Mailgun has stopped (§605, §622), is skipped at once. The row says «Trimis prin cealaltă cale»; a line `[email-relay] … left by gmail` goes to the function log (the house's operations log), an audit row `email_road.failed_over` names the roads (no actor, never a word or an address), and each Administrator and Superadministrator is emailed once per club day per road, and once per club day per form when a message is lost (`RELAY_NOTICE`, composed in RO or EN by the person's own language; the list on the page has every message). (4) **A pin, but a bounded one: no double send by design, no loss by default.** A refused address is the recipient's, not the road's: BOUNCED, the other road is not tried, the Administrators are told. A send whose connection broke where the service may already have the message is *ambiguous* and pins the message to that road **for three tries** (`RELAY_PIN_RELEASE_AFTER`) — long enough for a slow success to land, no longer. Neither service can be asked: Gmail has no lookup over SMTP, Mailgun's API does not dedupe on `v:idempotency_key` and Gmail does not on `X-Outbox-Key`, so retrying the same road duplicates exactly as much as the other road would, and a pin that never let go turned a possible duplicate into a delay and then a loss — a hanging Mailgun never failed over, and the words were deleted at twenty-four hours while Gmail was healthy. After three failures on the pinned road, or at once when it is stopped and the other may carry the message, the roads take turns as for any failure; a message that may not take the other road (Girl Zone without the tick) stays on its own and is given up on at twenty-four hours with the Administrators told. A person's message that arrives twice is better than one that does not arrive. To make the distinction real the adapters say what they know, **by what Nodemailer really gives**: every connection-level error carries the command `CONN` whatever the phase, so the command says nothing, and the message and the kind do — a connect or greeting timeout, a refused or unresolved connection, TLS, a refused login and the server's own answer to an envelope command or to the message are before acceptance; a plain `Timeout`, a socket error on a connection that was made and a connection closed with no answer from the server are ambiguous (proved against a fake SMTP server that takes the body and never answers `250`, pooled and single). Mailgun's `fetch` failures are ambiguous unless the request certainly never reached it (DNS, refused, connect timeout), and both roads now honour `replyTo`, `replyToName` and `noReplyTo` (Gmail ignored them for the outbox). (4b) **The roads' state tells the truth.** The state keeps the real code of a Gmail refusal (`smtp EAUTH`), never the sender's generic «not taking messages in this batch»; the club's own cap deferral and a Gmail that is not configured are not a road failing; a road rings (`emailRoadDown`) only while its failures have gone on for over an hour **and are still coming** — one failure on a quiet road never rings — and a Gmail account taken away clears its row.

(5) **Girl Zone.** A message for her person that Mailgun cannot carry goes by Gmail only if the club ticked «Dacă Mailgun pică, trimite prin Gmail-ul clubului» on «Pagini» → «Contact» (a real tick, off by default, with the note that whoever reads the club's mailbox sees it in Sent; stored in the setting's JSON, `safety.fallbackToGmail`, audited) AND the privacy notice in force names Gmail for her messages (`{{feedbackSafetyGmail}}`): the tick is greyed with its reason until it does, and an unticked message waits for Mailgun — never by the club's mailbox. Her message by the Gmail the club chose for her may be taken over by Mailgun, the road the notice promised her. The contact form and the three ordinary forms fall back by default. (6) **A day without a road.** A transient refusal is never the end of an ordinary email (§622), but this is somebody's words in a table: after twenty-four hours the message is FAILED, its words deleted, the Administrators emailed («Un mesaj de pe site nu a putut fi trimis»), an audit row `email_relay.lost` written; «Reîncearcă emailurile eșuate» does not put it back (nothing is left to send) and `/api/health` does not count it as `failed` (a 503 nothing can clear for a week) — it has its own «Sarcini» row for seven days. (7) **The roads' state.** `platform_settings.emailRoadStatus` holds, per road, since when it has been failing and its last short error code (written only on a failure and when a failing road works again, by the notifications' sender too — `withRoadStatus`); the last success is read from the outbox. `/devs` → «Stare» shows each road's last success and last refusal; «Setări» → «Emailuri» → «Mesaje de pe site» shows both and one row per message of the last seven days with its road, how it left, its tries, the words' state; `/admin/tasks` carries the red rows `emailRoadDown` (a road failing over an hour) and `relayLost`. (8) **One rule for both roads on QA.** The environment's allowlist now judges Gmail's road as Mailgun's: a recipient it does not name is captured, with 0 recipients on the row. The contact form's Gmail messages also count against Gmail's daily cap (§443), like every outbox row.

**Kept.** The outbox table, its claim and send path for the twenty-seven notification types, the Mailgun stop and the Gmail fallback (§622), Gmail's cap and pace (§443), the canonicalizer, hashed single-use links, `APP_BASE_URL` for every address, no new dependency (Nodemailer and the Mailgun `fetch` adapter as they were), no legal text in effect changed.

**Rejected.** Sending the message first and queueing only a failure — it would leave `/admin/emails` blind to the happy path, which is what hid the cause. A second table for visitors' messages — the owner asked for one outbox. Looking a message up at Gmail or Mailgun to resolve an ambiguous send — Gmail has no API for it from SMTP, and Mailgun's logs key is a developer's, not the app's. Failing over on a bounce — the other road would bounce the same address and a second provider would see a bad recipient. Keeping the words after a failure «for the Administrators to resend» — the notice promises seconds, and the owner's own wording was «se șterge». Gating the queue on the privacy notice — a message must never be lost to wait for a text, and gating it would undo the owner's first ask; the marker `{{relayQueue}}` and its `/admin/tasks` row only tell the club, and the lawyer reads the sentence when the club approves. Pruning the relay's trace rows sooner than the outbox's ninety days — they hold a recipient (the club's mailbox, or Girl Zone's person) and the road, never a word or the sender; left as they are. Dropping the optional webhook that would settle a pinned Mailgun row as sent — a second source of truth for a rare case the bounded pin already covers.

**Decided by the dispatcher on the owner's «YOLO»** (the owner may overturn): two failures before the other road; twenty-four hours before a message is given up on; an ambiguous send is pinned to its road for three tries and then the other road carries it; the queue is not gated on the privacy notice, whose new marker `{{relayQueue}}` only opens a `/admin/tasks` row; the notice says «seconds, three days at the very most»; the allowlist applies to Gmail; failed messages are not part of `/api/health`'s `failed`; the Administrators' notices are emails composed by the relay (no new template in the email editor); the contact form stays Gmail-first.

**Amends** §149 (the contact form's message is an outbox row, no longer sent from the request and never kept nowhere), §676 and §772 (the forms' delivery and the card's footer: kept only until delivered; a road is the club's choice, and the other road carries it when it is down), §622 (the Administrators' notice and the «Sarcini» rows for a road that is down, and the transient-refusal rule's one exception: a visitor's message is given up on after a day), §443 (the contact form's messages count against Gmail's cap; the adapter reads a timeout before `DATA` as not accepted) and §68 (a visitor's message leaves after its response whatever the delivery timing).

**Tests.** Unit `road-failover.test.ts` (the rule as a table: failover after two, both ways, turns, the pin, the stopped road, what each answer means), `relay-adapters.test.ts` (the Gmail failure shapes Nodemailer really gives — proved against a fake SMTP server that never answers `250`, that drops the socket after the body, that never greets and a port that refuses, pooled and single — the Reply-To of both roads, Mailgun's request that never reached it), `feedback-fallback-tick.test.ts` (the tick, greyed and carried, the self-recipient warning, `fallbackAllowedFor`), `owner-tasks.test.ts` (the three rows), `branches.test.ts` and `identity-choice.test.ts` (Girl Zone's wording with the tick), the i18n guards. Integration `notifications/relay.test.ts` (PGlite: queue and deliver, the words gone; Mailgun to Gmail and back with the mark, the audit row, the log line and the notices in both languages; a 401 as a service failure; a spent allowance as all attempts at once; a stopped road skipped; a bounce ends BOUNCED with no other road; an ambiguous send keeps its road for three tries and then the other carries it, with a stopped pinned road giving way and a Girl Zone message with no other road given up on after a day; the notices once per club day; Girl Zone without the tick never leaves Mailgun; Gmail's pace is no failure; twenty-four hours; a notice raises none; the main claim, «Reîncearcă…» and `/api/health` leave it alone; the page's read has no address or word), `notifications/road-status.test.ts` (the ring: one old failure is not red), `notifications/relay-roads.test.ts` (the production wiring over the real sender, ledger and state: the code kept, the cap, the stop), `feedback/submit.test.ts` and `contact/*.test.ts` (the services queue; the relay delivers; refused roads answer «sent»; the tick saved, audited, kept when greyed). E2E `feedback.spec.ts` and `contact.spec.ts` through the outbox and the capture sink.

**The owner's questions, answered by the dispatcher on his «YOLO»** (he may overturn any): *Should the release wait for the new privacy notice to be approved?* No — a message must not be lost for a text; approve the notice (`/admin/legal`, the same sitting as the other texts of the release; a lawyer reads the contact and feedback paragraphs of section 5 first) and `relayQueueNotice` closes by itself. *Should Girl Zone's fallback tick stay off until then?* Yes — the tick is greyed until the notice names her Gmail road (`{{feedbackSafetyGmail}}`), and while it is on the public line says her message may leave by the club's mailbox when the email service is down (never «doar la …»). *Which check tells whether Gmail carried a QA post?* `/devs` → «Stare» now names the road each message left by, and «Setări» → «Emailuri» → «Mesaje de pe site» one row per message.

**Confirmed by the owner, 2026-10-15 13:20:** the messages had arrived — a Gmail filter had filed them out of the Inbox. No transport failure and no configuration change; what was missing was the site's record of where a message went, which this release adds.
changelogLine: - **«Scrie-ne» and «Spune-ne ceva» through the outbox, with failover** — a visitor's message is queued, sent at once after the response, and carried by the other road (Gmail or Mailgun) when the chosen one fails twice; its words are deleted the moment it leaves (three days at the very most when no service works), a refused address is never retried elsewhere, a send that may already be delivered stays on its road for three tries and then the other carries it, and Girl Zone falls back to Gmail only with the club's tick and says so to the visitor; «Mesaje de pe site», `/devs` and «Sarcini» show each road's state and the Administrators are emailed when a road is down or a message is lost; `/admin/tasks` asks the club to approve the privacy notice that says so. What is proven about QA's «did not send by Gmail» is that no refusal was logged: §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends criteria 3, 6, 27, 28 and 29. Given a valid post of «Scrie-ne» or of any «Spune-ne ceva» form, when the action answers, then the message is one row of `email_outbox` (type `CONTACT_MESSAGE` or `FEEDBACK_MESSAGE`, no participant, no registration) carrying the road the club chose in `road` and its words in `payload_json`, answered «trimis» whatever the road does next, and sent after the response by the relay (`notifications/relay.ts`), never from the request; on delivery the words are deleted (`payload_json` = `{"deleted":true}`, `body_deleted_at` set) and the row keeps its road, the road it left by, the time and the provider's id, and no address or word of any message (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a visitor's message whose chosen road has failed it twice with a failure that is the service's (a refused login, a 5xx, no connection, a spent allowance or a pause) — never the recipient's — when the relay next sends it, then the other road carries it, both ways, Mailgun to Gmail and Gmail to Mailgun, once the other road is configured and not stopped; the row's `transport` differs from its `road` and the page says «Trimis prin cealaltă cale», one function-log line and one `email_road.failed_over` audit row (no actor, no word, no address) are written, and every Administrator and Superadministrator is emailed once a day per road in the language of their own row (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a refused recipient address the message ends BOUNCED and no other road is tried; given a failure after which the service may already have the message (a plain timeout, a socket error on a connection that was made, a connection closed with no answer, once the message was on its way), the message is pinned to that road for three tries and retried there, after which — or at once when that road is stopped — the other road carries it when the message may take it, and one idempotency key rides both roads; given a visitor's message no road has carried in twenty-four hours, it is FAILED, its words are deleted, the Administrators are emailed and an `email_relay.lost` audit row is written, and «Reîncearcă emailurile eșuate» does not put it back (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given Girl Zone's person as the reader, when Mailgun cannot carry her message, then it goes by Gmail only while the club's tick «Dacă Mailgun pică, trimite prin Gmail-ul clubului» is on (a checkbox, off by default, drawn only while her road is Mailgun, with the note that the club's mailbox readers see the message in Sent, greyed with its reason and keeping what is saved while Gmail is missing or the notice in force does not name `{{feedbackSafetyGmail}}`, and not newly savable then) AND that notice names it; otherwise it waits for Mailgun; while the tick is in force the form's line, the identity choice and the sent page say her message may leave by the club's mailbox when the email service is down instead of «doar la …»; the other three forms and the contact form fall back by default (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given «Setări» → «Emailuri», `/devs` → «Stare» and «Sarcini», when they render, then «Mesaje de pe site» lists the visitors' messages of the last seven days with their form, status, road chosen, road they left by, tries, what each road answered and whether the words are kept or deleted — no address and no word — beside each road's last success, last refusal and, while failing, since when; `/devs` shows the same per road, with the real code of the last refusal (`smtp EAUTH`); and «Sarcini» carries the red rows `emailRoadDown` (a road whose failures have gone on for over an hour and are still coming, named with its last code) and `relayLost` (a message given up on in seven days), both in Romanian and English (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a form whose recipient is the very Gmail account that sends (by the canonicalizer, never a string compare) and whose road is Gmail, when «Pagini» → «Contact» renders, then a warning beside the recipient says Gmail may keep such a message in Sent only; the privacy notice template's contact and feedback paragraphs say, through the marker `{{relayQueue}}`, that the platform keeps a message only until it leaves (seconds, three days at the very most) and then deletes it, and that the other road carries it when the chosen one is down, in both languages; and `/admin/tasks` carries the row `relayQueueNotice` until a notice naming it is in force in both languages, with the queue running meanwhile (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 1. The outbox also carries the visitors' messages (`CONTACT_MESSAGE`, `FEEDBACK_MESSAGE`) and the platform's own notices about a road (`RELAY_NOTICE`) through a worker of their own: the notifications' claim never takes them, `/api/health` counts them as waiting and, after ninety minutes, overdue, but not as `failed`, and the road each row asked for, the failures each road gave it and the deletion of its words are columns of `email_outbox` (migration `0162_outbox_road_and_failures`, expand only) (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a Gmail connection or greeting that never answered (`Connection timeout`, `Greeting never received`), a refused or unresolved connection, or a failure that names an SMTP command ahead of `DATA`, when the Gmail road reports it, then it is a failure before acceptance — the sender hands the message to Mailgun at once for a group the club put on Gmail — and every other timeout (`Timeout`), socket error on a connection that was made and connection closed with no answer from the server stays "may have been accepted" (Nodemailer labels all of them `CONN`, so the message decides, not the command); given a Mailgun request that never reached it (DNS, refused, connect timeout) the result is not ambiguous, and any other network failure is (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: every mail through the outbox; failover between Mailgun and Gmail
